course_title: Anatomy & Neuroanatomy Fundamentals for Speech Pathologists

learning_outcomes.description: Describe the main anatomical structures of the head, neck and thorax involved in human communication and swallowing.
Associate anatomical structures and their function to typical communication and swallowing processes.
Explain the role of key sensory and motor systems in typical communication and swallowing processes.
Integrate various anatomical structures and their function of the head, neck, and thorax to predict functional deficits resulting from altered anatomy.
Recognise and adhere to ethical principles when participating in human cadaveric learning.
Effectively communicate anatomical structures and functions in typical communication and swallowing processes with others.

assessments.task_description:
In-class spotter quizzes will cover content (practical and lectures) from previous weeks. Quizzes are completed at the beginning of each practical class.

  • Each quiz consists of 10 multiple-choice questions using anatomical models and specimens.
  • Students will have approximately 45 seconds to complete each question.
  • A total of four (4) quizzes will be conducted across the semester.
  • Each quiz contributes 10%, for a total of 40% of the final course grade.
  • These quizzes are closed-book and should be completed independently, without access to notes or electronic devices.
  • Students will have access to the quiz questions, pinned specimens and correct answers for review immediately after the quiz during scheduled class.

Additional information is available on the Blackboard site and will be covered during the course introduction.

Have your UQ student ID card available for all your quizzes.

This assessment task is to be completed in-person. The use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) or Machine Translation (MT) tools will not be permitted. Any attempted use of AI or MT may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct.

assessments.assessment_title: End of Semester Interactive Oral Exam (Viva)
assessments.task_description:
The Interactive Oral Assessment (IOA or Viva) is a single, 8-minute interview with an examiner. Students will have 10 minutes of planning time where they will be exposed to an unseen scenario. The examiner will act as a standardised patient/actor during the assessment. The student will take on a role of a speech pathology student explaining an anatomy concept to the examiner, role-playing as one of the following: healthcare worker, practice educator / tutor, patient, or member of the public. The exact scenario will be detailed in the question stem.

The exam will be a closed book invigilated exam held on campus. Due to the nature of the exam, the exact exam time on the day will be confirmed at a closer date. Students are recommended to block out the morning of the exam date. Further information about the exam will be provided on Blackboard.

The exam will cover all the content from Modules 1-4.

Have your UQ student ID card available for all your exams. This exam is recorded.
